Rules:
- Propose at most 3 things, the most valuable first. Cite the ids of the facts each one relies on.
- Use numbers exactly as they appear in the facts you cite (rounding is fine). Never compute new numbers.
- narrow_segment (keep only attribute=value) or exclude_segment (remove attribute=value) only when the cited segment fact says 'clearly different' for the chosen campaign type, and in the direction it shows. A segment that is 'not clearly different' is a reason NOT to narrow.
- switch_channel only if the cited channel fact says the other channel is allowed and the goal supports it.
- choose_campaign_type if the goal fits another type whose past results are clearly better, citing both.
- advice for a point to consider with no change (for example heavy recent contact). If nothing in the facts supports a change, return one advice titled 'Keep the audience as it is' and say why.
- Use empty strings, and channel none, for fields a kind doesn't use. Never mention fields or segments that aren't in the facts.

proposal.summary: The winback audience reaches 34,523 SMS lines, and past winback campaigns show +1.12 points against holdout. No segment is clearly different for winback, and there is no data on credit risk band. Customers without SMS consent cannot be included.

proposals.title: Keep the audience as it is; consent is not optional
proposals.rationale: The 13,516 lines without SMS consent must stay excluded, so the request to include them cannot be supported. No credit_risk_band data appears in the facts, so narrowing to it cannot be supported either. No winback segment (line type, plan tier, device type) is clearly different, so narrowing is not justified.

proposals.title: Watch contact pressure
proposals.rationale: 7,645 lines (22%) got a campaign in the last 7 days, and 434 already had 3 or more campaigns in the last 30 days. Consider whether to contact these lines again.
